name: tag-group-error-missing
description: A tag has tagGroup or topLevelTagGroup attribute, but is not enclosed in parentheses.
common_causes: Tags requiring groups not enclosed in parentheses
topLevelTagGroup tags not at top level
Multiple topLevelTagGroup tags in same group
Temporal tags not properly grouped
Definition tags not in required group structure
explanation: Certain HED tags have schema attributes requiring them to appear in tag groups. Tags with 'tagGroup' must be in parentheses, 'topLevelTagGroup' tags must be in top-level groups, and only specific combinations are allowed.
correction_strategy: Ensure required tags are properly grouped according to their attributes

correction_examples.explanation: Enclosed Definition tag in required parentheses
Put Onset in group with required definition
Properly grouped temporal tags according to their requirements

correction_patterns: Ensure topLevelTagGroup tags are at top level
Limit to one topLevelTagGroup per group (except Duration+Delay)
Group temporal tags with required companions
fix_instructions: 1. Identify tags with grouping requirements from schema
2. Check if tag is properly enclosed in parentheses
3. Verify top-level tags are at correct level
4. Ensure proper companions for temporal tags
5. Check for multiple topLevelTagGroup violations
validation_hints: Consult schema for tag grouping attributes
Ensure temporal tag companions are present

name: tag-group-error-not-top-level
description: A tag with the topLevelTagGroup does not appear at a HED tag group at the top level in an assembled HED annotation.
common_causes: Top-level tags nested too deeply in groups
Temporal tags incorrectly grouped below top level
Extra parentheses around top-level tags
Misunderstanding of top-level tag requirements
Incorrect nesting of temporal or context tags
explanation: Tags with topLevelTagGroup attribute (like Duration, Onset, Offset, Event-context) must appear at the top level of tag groups, not nested within other groups.
correction_strategy: Move top-level tags to proper group depth

correction_examples.explanation: Removed extra parentheses to make Duration top-level
Moved Onset to top-level of group

correction_patterns: Remove extra parentheses around top-level tags
Ensure temporal tags are at top group level
fix_instructions: 1. Identify tags with topLevelTagGroup attribute
2. Check their current nesting level
3. Remove extra parentheses to make them top-level
4. Verify proper group structure
5. Test tag hierarchy compliance
validation_hints: Check nesting depth of temporal tags
Ensure Event-context is at top level
Look for extra parentheses around top-level tags

name: tag-group-error-deferred-in-splice
description: A tag with the topLevelTagGroup does not appear at a HED tag group at the top level in an assembled HED annotation.
common_causes: Top-level tags nested in column splice operations
Deferred evaluation causing incorrect tag positioning
Column references creating improper nesting
Sidecar substitution breaking top-level requirements
Complex column dependencies affecting tag hierarchy
explanation: When columns are spliced together in sidecar processing, tags with topLevelTagGroup attribute must still end up at the top level of the final assembled annotation. The group rules of a reserved tag are checked on the assembled annotation, so (Duration/3 s, {other}) and (Onset, {other}) are valid when the other column supplies the inner group or the anchor, and invalid when the substitution gives the Duration group two inner groups.
correction_strategy: Restructure sidecar to maintain top-level positioning

correction_examples.explanation: Prevented Duration from being nested during splice

correction_patterns: Restructure column HED to avoid nesting top-level tags
Use proper grouping in sidecar column definitions
Ensure column substitution maintains tag hierarchy
fix_instructions: 1. Identify problematic column splice operations
2. Examine how columns combine in final annotation
3. Restructure sidecar to prevent top-level tag nesting
4. Test assembled annotation structure
5. Verify top-level tag positioning
validation_hints: Trace column substitution effects on nesting
Verify top-level tags remain at top level
specification_reference: 3.2.9.3. Sidecar curly braces (rule 9); 3.2.8. Reserved tags (rule 5); Appendix B TAG_GROUP_ERROR b

name: multiple-top-level-tags-in-same-group
description: Multiple tags with the topLevelTagGroup attribute appear in the same top-level tag group. (Delay and Duration are allowed to be in the same topLevelTagGroup).
common_causes: Multiple context tags in single group
Combining incompatible temporal tags
Multiple top-level tags where only one allowed
Misunderstanding top-level tag exclusivity rules
Incorrect grouping of Event-context with temporal tags
explanation: Most top-level tags are mutually exclusive within a group. Only Delay and Duration can coexist in the same top-level group. Other combinations violate cardinality constraints.
correction_strategy: Separate incompatible top-level tags into different groups

correction_examples.explanation: Separated Onset and Event-context into different groups
Moved Event-context to separate group from temporal tags

correction_patterns: Create separate groups for incompatible top-level tags
fix_instructions: 1. Identify groups with multiple top-level tags
2. Check if combination is allowed (only Delay+Duration)
3. Separate incompatible tags into different groups
4. Verify proper group structure
5. Test cardinality compliance
validation_hints: Only one top-level tag per group (except Delay+Duration)
Check for multiple temporal tags in same group

name: tag-group-error-event-context-contents
description: An `Event-context` group contains, besides the `Event-context` tag, only tag groups, one per ongoing event process.
common_causes: Placing the tags of an ongoing event directly in the Event-context group instead of in their own group
Hand-written Event-context groups
explanation: An Event-context group has the form (Event-context, (content-group), ...). Each content group holds the tags of one ongoing event process and is generated by tools. A bare tag beside Event-context does not belong to any process and is an error.
correction_strategy: Wrap the tags of each ongoing process in their own group inside the Event-context group

correction_examples.explanation: Red is wrapped in its own content group

correction_patterns: Wrap each bare tag in the Event-context group in parentheses
Let tools generate Event-context groups rather than writing them by hand
fix_instructions: 1. List the members of the Event-context group
2. Wrap every member that is a tag, other than Event-context itself, in a group
3. Check that each group describes one ongoing event process
validation_hints: Only Event-context may be a bare tag in its group
Any number of content groups, including none, is allowed

name: tag-group-error-event-context-braces
description: An Event-context group contains a sidecar column reference ({column}). Column references may not appear in an Event-context group; they may appear beside it.
common_causes: Assembling the ongoing-event contents of an Event-context group from another column with curly braces
Copying a pattern that is valid in a Duration or Onset group into an Event-context group
explanation: An Event-context group lists the event processes that are ongoing at an event marker, and tools generate it with every definition and column reference already expanded. A curly brace column reference inside the group is therefore not allowed, although references are allowed in Duration, Delay, Onset, Offset, and Inset groups. Usually the Event-context group should be left to tools altogether.
correction_strategy: Remove the column reference from the Event-context group: write the content group out, or move the reference outside the group

correction_examples.explanation: The content group is written out
The reference moves outside the group

specification_reference: 3.2.8. Reserved tags (table row Event-context, rule 5); 3.2.9.3. Sidecar curly braces (rule 5); Appendix B TAG_GROUP_ERROR e
